reference_text:
Welcome to the course. We will work through each concept carefully, connect the
ideas step by step, and use practical examples to make technical topics easier
to understand. When we introduce a new method, focus first on the problem it
solves and why it is useful. For example, in machine learning, features are the
information we give the model, while the target is what we want it to predict.
Now consider a simple question: what changes when the data contains missing
values? We will think through the reason and then look at the code. In Python,
we can inspect the data, run one small step at a time, and explain what the
result means. The goal is to understand the logic, not simply memorize syntax.

slides.title: Cleaning & EDA
slides.transcript: Welcome to Module 12. This module focuses on data cleaning and exploratory data analysis. Before formal analysis or modeling, we need to understand missingness, duplicate records, incorrect data types, inconsistent categories, unusual values, and the general shape of the data.

slides.title: How to use this page
slides.transcript:
Use this lesson actively. Read the idea first and make a prediction before running any code. When a Python cell is available, click Run, inspect the output, and then change one small value or condition. Run it again and explain what changed. This predict, run, modify, and explain cycle is more useful than copying a finished example.

[tts-break]

Do not treat cleaning as automatic deletion or filling. Measure the problem first, decide what the value means, apply a defensible rule, and then validate the data again.

[tts-break]

Before moving on, explain the main idea in one sentence without reading the slide. That quick explanation is a useful check that the concept is becoming reusable knowledge.
